notes: Voice adds the channel the call arrives over. Everything else is inherited from universal.json; only the axes named here are overridden.

axes.name: channel
axes.label: Channel
axes.of: the conditions the call arrives under
axes.baseline: a quiet room and a clean line

settings.name: street
settings.guidance: Calling from a pavement. Traffic under the voice, and they raise their own to compete with it.

settings.name: vehicle
settings.guidance: Hands-free in a moving car. Road noise, cabin echo, and attention on the road rather than the call.

settings.name: crowd
settings.guidance: A busy public place. Other voices carry, and some of what the agent hears was never said to it.

settings.name: dropping
settings.unwired: no packet-loss or jitter injection exists in the voice path, so this setting would change nothing about the call
settings.guidance: A failing mobile connection: words disappear mid-sentence and confirmations have to survive it.

settings.name: interrupted
settings.unwired: interruption is enabled for every call rather than per scenario, so this setting is not a variation of anything
settings.guidance: Talks over the agent rather than waiting for it to finish.

axes.name: who
axes.label: Who
axes.baseline: verified account holder, ordinary literacy, speaking the default language

settings.name: senior
settings.guidance: An older caller, less fluent with the product's vocabulary. They answer in narrative rather than in the field the agent asked for, and they take longer to get to it.

settings.name: second-language
settings.guidance: Speaks the service's language as a second language. Comprehension is fine, phrasing is not native, and an accent the recogniser handles less well is part of the test.

settings.name: on-someone-behalf
settings.guidance: Calling for the account holder, not the account holder. Everything they know is second hand, and some of it is wrong.

settings.name: unverified
settings.guidance: Cannot or will not complete verification on this call. What the agent still does for them is the graded behaviour.
